clue.text: Oil producer has girl ferrying river sprite around

indicators.note: to ferry is to carry across, so the girl's word holds the other letters within it

parts.note: lass is a girl

indicators.note: around tells us to turn the river-and-sprite string to face the other way

parts.note: R is the map abbreviation for river
a gnome is a small sprite of folklore

explanation.surface: A girl carries a water spirit about while some plant or well produces oil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oil producer' suggests a well or a rig, but it is a plant; 'river' gives just its map letter here.
explanation.definitionFit: Lemongrass is a tropical grass whose leaves are distilled for an aromatic essential oil.

clue.text: Reluctant auctioneer's eighth item?

parts.note: an auctioneer's item for sale is a lot
H is the eighth letter of the alphabet

explanation.surface: A question about what an auctioneer brings out eighth in a sale.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one lot number; split it into the auctioneer's LOT and the alphabet's eighth letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Loth is a variant spelling of loath, meaning unwilling or disinclined.

clue.text: Policy statement complicated by means of it?

indicators.note: complicated suggests the letters of these three words are tangled into a new order

explanation.surface: A political programme muddled by the very methods it proposes.
explanation.definitionFit: A manifesto is a published declaration of a party's aims and intended policies.

clue.text: Conservationists in state bound to be heard

parts.note: a nation is a state

indicators.note: to be heard means we want a word that sounds like the phrase, not its spelling

parts.note: bound means tied up, all trussed

explanation.surface: Environmentalists in some country are obliged to make their voices heard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bound' is not 'obliged' but 'all trussed', which spoken aloud gives the second word's ending after AL.
explanation.definitionFit: The National Trust is a British charity that preserves historic houses, gardens and countryside.

clue.text: One should occupy immovable property in fact

indicators.note: should occupy says the numeral's letter moves into and sits inside the property word

parts.note: realty is real estate, land and buildings that cannot be moved
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone ought really to be living in a building that cannot be moved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in fact' reads as a phrase, but 'in' is a link and 'fact' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Reality is what actually exists, the truth of things, so it is a synonym of fact.

clue.text: Island man not completely absorbed in Sanskrit works

indicators.note: absorbed in means held inside the word for the Sanskrit texts

parts.note: sutras are ancient Sanskrit texts of aphorisms

indicators.note: not completely tells us to drop the last letter of the word

parts.note: taken as written before trimming

explanation.surface: An islander is partly lost in reading Sanskrit literature.
explanation.walkthrough: Sutras are the aphoristic teaching texts of Hindu and Buddhist tradition, written in Sanskrit.
explanation.definitionFit: Sumatra is a large Indonesian island in the western part of the archipelago.

clue.text: Republican bundled into taxi that moves sideways

indicators.note: bundled into says the abbreviation is pushed inside the vehicle word

parts.note: a cab is a taxi

explanation.surface: A US politician is shoved into a cab that then skids sideways.
explanation.definitionFit: A crab is the crustacean famous for its sideways scuttling walk.

clue.text: Length adding to value in clawed animal

indicators.note: adding to says the abbreviation is attached at the end of the other word

parts.note: to rate is to value, and a rate is a value

explanation.surface: A claim that extra length increases the worth of some clawed beast.
explanation.definitionFit: The ratel, or honey badger, is an African mammal with long, powerful digging claws.

clue.text: Wearing nothing fantastic asset round north ocean region

indicators.note: round says those letters go around the abbreviation for north

parts.note: bare means naked, wearing nothing

indicators.note: fantastic hints the letters of the next word are wildly rearranged

parts.note: N is the compass abbreviation for north

explanation.surface: A naked investor's wonderful holding surrounds a northern stretch of sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ocean region' is fair because this sea is a marginal part of the Arctic Ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: The Barents Sea is the part of the Arctic Ocean north of Norway and Russia.

clue.text: 15 spiking a Spanish red? That's the principle

indicators.note: to spike a drink is to slip something into it, so the drug's letter goes inside

parts.note: tent is an old name for a deep red Spanish wine
the answer to 15 is ecstasy, the drug abbreviated E

explanation.surface: A drug slipped into a glass of Spanish red, presented as a guiding rule.
explanation.walkthrough: Tent is a dark red wine from Spain, from Spanish tinto; E is ecstasy, the answer to 15.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenet is a belief or doctrine held as true, which is what a principle is.

clue.text: Old school graduates change trousers

indicators.note: to trouser is to pocket, so the change word takes the graduates inside it

parts.note: to alter is to change
MA is a Master of Arts graduate, so two graduates give MAMA

explanation.surface: Former pupils of an old school switch their trousers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trousers' looks like clothing but is a verb meaning pockets.
explanation.definitionFit: One's alma mater is the school or university one formerly attended.

clue.text: Space probes face constant thundering in explosive aftermath

indicators.note: probes says the space word comes pushing in right behind the face word

parts.note: mush is slang for the face
room is space
C is the scientific symbol for a constant, such as the speed of light
thundering means very loud

explanation.surface: Space probes encounter constant noise in the wake of an explosion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Space probes' reads as spacecraft, but space is ROOM and 'face' is the slang MUSH.
explanation.definitionFit: A mushroom cloud is the tall billowing column of smoke left after a nuclear blast.

clue.text: Trader being in no hurry to plug pink publication

indicators.note: to plug is to fill a hole, so the animal sits inside the newspaper's letters

parts.note: the Financial Times, FT, is printed on pink paper
the slow loris is a famously slow-moving primate

explanation.surface: A relaxed shopkeeper promotes a pink-coloured newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being in no hurry' is a creature, the slow loris; the FT is the British financial newspaper printed on pink paper.
explanation.definitionFit: A florist is a shopkeeper who sells flowers and plants, a kind of retailer.

clue.text: Valediction cut short for Athenian statesman

indicators.note: cut short tells us to drop the final letter of the farewell

parts.note: so long is a farewell, a valediction

explanation.surface: A farewell speech made brief for a statesman of ancient Athens.
explanation.definitionFit: Solon was the sixth-century BC lawgiver who reformed the Athenian constitution.

clue.text: See time in Rome spoiled by Scots rozzers

indicators.note: spoiled shows the combined letters are ruined and rearranged

parts.note: polis is the Scottish word for police; rozzers is British slang for police

explanation.surface: Look: a spell in Rome ruined by Scottish police.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' looks like the verb but is a bishop's see; a metropolis is a metropolitan bishop's see.
explanation.definitionFit: In church usage a metropolis is the chief city of a province and seat of its archbishop.

clue.text: Yes! Cats can produce bliss!

indicators.note: can produce suggests the two words' letters are reworked into something new

explanation.surface: An excited cry that cats can bring sheer happiness.
explanation.definitionFit: Ecstasy is an overwhelming feeling of joy, the same rapture as bliss.

clue.text: Fit ace rugby forwards carrying ball

parts.note: A is the card abbreviation for ace

indicators.note: carrying says the forwards hold the ball letter within them

parts.note: props are front-row forwards in rugby
O is shaped like a ball

explanation.surface: Excellent fit rugby forwards running with the ball.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fit' looks like an adjective for athletes but means suitable, the sense of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Apropos means appropriate or pertinent, and fit can mean suitable to the occasion.

clue.text: Leaving starter, insect dives into dish that's smoked

indicators.note: dives into puts the trimmed insect inside the dish

parts.note: paella is a Spanish rice dish

indicators.note: leaving starter says the first letter of the insect is dropped

parts.note: a gnat is a small flying insect

explanation.surface: An insect, skipping the first course, plunges into a dish of smoked food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaving starter' makes NAT, which 'dives into' PAELLA; 'smoked' is not cooking but cigars.
explanation.definitionFit: A panatella is a long slender cigar, the kind of thing people light up.

clue.text: Chicken and egg in roll?

indicators.note: in places the egg letter within the list word

parts.note: a roster is a roll or list of names
O is shaped like an egg

explanation.surface: The old chicken-and-egg question, recast as a bread roll filling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'roll' looks like bread, but it is a list.
explanation.definitionFit: A rooster is a male domestic fowl, a cockerel, so a kind of chicken.

clue.text: Polish trick to get across international boundary

indicators.note: to get across says the trick word is placed beyond the international letter

parts.note: to rub is to polish
a con is a trick or swindle

explanation.surface: A Polish swindle to cross an international frontier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' with its capital looks like the nationality but is the verb rub.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rubicon was the river Caesar crossed, so it now means any point of no return or limit.

clue.text: Girl who's promised cake?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a junior Girl Guide
second meaning: a small square of rich chocolate cake

explanation.surface: A girl who has been promised a cake.
explanation.walkthrough: Brownies are the junior branch of the Girl Guides, and new members make a formal promise.
explanation.definitionFit: The same word names a young Guide member and a dense chocolate traybake.

clue.text: Cheese as seconds consumed in old club

indicators.note: consumed in means eaten up inside, so the letters go within the cheese

parts.note: Brie is a soft French cheese

explanation.surface: Cheese eaten as second helpings in a long-established club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'club' is a golf club, not a society.
explanation.definitionFit: The brassie was an old wooden golf club, roughly a two-wood, with a brass sole.

clue.text: Died in South American country once placed in ambush

indicators.note: in places the died letter within the country

parts.note: Peru is in South America

explanation.surface: Someone died in Peru, ambushed long ago.
explanation.definitionFit: Perdu is an archaic military term for a soldier lying hidden in a dangerous post.

clue.text: Headless chicken or crow

indicators.note: headless says the first letter of the word is cut off

parts.note: craven means cowardly, like chicken

explanation.surface: Is it a headless chicken or a crow?
explanation.walkthrough: 'chicken' is the adjective for cowardly, not the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The raven is the largest member of the crow family of black birds.

clue.text: Panda car crashing blocks route taken by police

indicators.note: blocks means the rearranged car sits in the middle of the route, obstructing it

parts.note: a beat is a police officer's patrol route

indicators.note: crashing shows the vehicle's letters are wrecked into a new order

explanation.surface: A British police car crashes and blocks the patrol route.
explanation.walkthrough: A panda car is British slang for a small police patrol car, but here 'Panda' is the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: Bearcat is another name for the red panda, as well as the binturong.

clue.text: Those last in triremes at sea may remain behind

indicators.note: those last in asks for the final letter of each following word

explanation.surface: The rearmost rowers in ancient warships at sea might stay put.
explanation.definitionFit: To stay is to remain in a place rather than leave with others.

clue.text: Lust, vice and crime essentially written about in old law book

indicators.note: written about suggests the letters are scattered around and set down anew
essentially means the essence, the central letter of the word

explanation.surface: A lurid tale of lust, vice and crime recorded in an ancient legal text.
explanation.definitionFit: Leviticus is the third book of the Old Testament, largely a code of priestly law.

clue.text: Initially obstructive wife to enable young head-turner

indicators.note: initially picks out just the opening letter of the next word

parts.note: to let is to allow or enable

explanation.surface: A wife is at first obstructive but then lets a striking young person through.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head-turner' reads as an attractive person, but owls can turn their heads almost all the way round.
explanation.definitionFit: An owlet is a baby owl, a bird famed for swivelling its head.

clue.text: For pot, go to pot?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to pot a ball in snooker
second meaning: to decline or deteriorate

explanation.walkthrough: Both senses play on 'pot'; one is the snooker shot, the other the idiom for falling into ruin.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb covers sending a ball into a pocket and also sliding into a worse state.

clue.text: Say Van Gogh's content with chronicle being scandalous?

indicators.note: content means what is held within, so the outer letters of the name are discarded

parts.note: Van Gogh's first name was Vincent; say marks him as an example
a diary is a chronicle of events

explanation.surface: Van Gogh's letters recorded in a diary are presented as shocking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'content' takes the inner letters of VINCENT, giving INCEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Incendiary means inflammatory, provoking outrage; the question mark flags a loose fit with scandalous.
